title: How do we build a solid from its three views?
description: Identical cubes are stacked to match a top view, a front view and a side view. The board puts one column on every square of the top view, sets the heights from the front and side views, and then checks all three views.
teaching_notes: One idea: start from the top view, put a column on every square, then let the front and side views fix the heights. Watch for students who build from the front view alone.

source: Figure it Out (shadows and views, question 4)
video_script.why: The child builds a solid of identical cubes from its views by starting with the top view and setting heights from the other two.
video_script.substitution: Put a column on every top view square, then set the heights from the front view and the side view.
video_script.anchor: a top view of three squares in a row, a front view with column heights two, one and two, a side view of height two, and a pile of identical cubes
video_script.payoff_line: Put one column on every top view square, then set the heights from the front and side views

final_answer.value: put one column on every top view square, then set the heights from the front and side views
final_answer.spoken: put one column on every top view square, then set the heights from the front and side views

hold_back: Answer: put one column on every top view square, then set the heights from the front and side views
never_show: a column taller than the front view allows
maths_rules: stand-in views: top view a row of 3 squares; front view column heights 2, 1, 2 from left to right; side view a column of height 2
check: top view 3 squares; front view heights 2, 1, 2; side view tallest height 2
video_script.design: Three frames show the given views beside a pile of cubes. Columns grow on the three top squares, then stretch to the heights from the front view, and the side view is checked last.
open_questions: The three views of the book question are pictures that are not in the extracted text, so the video builds one solid from a set of views of the same kind and gives the method for any other set.
